supported_conclusions.conclusion: Channel table index is ((id >> 16) & 255)*17 + (id >> 24). AppProxy map IDs 0x02033204/0x02033203/0x02033212 select (3,2), index 53. Controller internal save event 0x3c is encoded as 0x0201001b and selects (1,2), index 19. Do not equate them or invent a controller forwarding edge.

Save request stores both key words at object+0x3a0/+0x3a4, emits event 0x3c through destination 2, then appends a 24-byte pending record under +0x36c mutex. Native command 0x2105 with exactly 16 payload bytes becomes event 0x836, retaining all four payload words. The selected result branch rejects zero key and checks +0x3b8 then +0x3d0 before +0x3a0. Both words must match. It removes pending by key before testing result==1, then clears the slot in the observed success/error branches.

A different nonzero key cannot take the selected controller slot branch. A reused key can pass these local checks; no epoch or map-flag equality check was seen in this branch, and earlier matching slots have priority. This does not prove practical collision, thread safety or the full stale-message policy. AppProxy series handling separately keys on the two request words; its legacy fallbacks are not a universal stale-result rejection barrier.

AppProxy send returns after SendPacket/logging without exposing a checked transport-success result. IPC writes 0x4c bytes to the selected channel; this is not native operation completion. Controller result handling retires request state, not a disk flush. Existing native persistence API success is snapshot acceptance, not all-file replacement or durable completion.
